clue.text: Does he take a chance, or just think about it?

definitions.text: Does he take a chance, or just think about it?

parts.words: Does he take a chance, or just think about it?
parts.note: one who gambles on markets, or merely someone who muses and theorises: both senses come from the same verb meaning to ponder or to gamble

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is a risk-taker or merely a dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gambles on price movements, or one who forms theories without firm evidence, is described by this noun.

clue.text: Aristocrat always preceded by a page

indicators.note: the page's letter is placed before the word for always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A nobleman who is forever attended by a young servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the nobility, such as a lord in the House of Lords, is called by this title.

clue.text: Pillar of the press?

parts.note: reads like a leading figure of journalism, but means both an upright architectural support and a regular newspaper feature

explanation.surface: A tribute to a pillar of journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an architectural pillar and a regular section of a newspaper.

clue.text: It results in a certain jumpiness among rugby players

definitions.text: It results in a certain jumpiness among rugby players

parts.words: It results in a certain jumpiness among rugby players
parts.note: jumpiness suggests nerves, but refers to players leaping to catch a ball thrown in from touch

explanation.surface: Rugby players getting nervous about something.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, forwards form parallel rows and jump to catch the ball thrown in from the touchline.

clue.text: Child has a point to convey

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E (east) is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A youngster with something to communicate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or transport something, a synonym of convey.

clue.text: Becomes exhausted and exits hurriedly

definitions.meaning: a supply that is used up is said to run out
someone who dashes from a room is said to run out

explanation.surface: Someone tired who leaves in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both a supply being used up and a person dashing outside.

clue.text: Davies seen playing a form of Rugby

indicators.note: playing suggests the rugby player in action, but signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welsh rugby player called Davies spotted on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Davies is a typically Welsh surname, so the surface paints a rugby player; DAVIES and SEEN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened variety of rugby union played by teams of seven is one form of the game.

clue.text: Manager we'd ordered to run the wild life reserve

definitions.text: to run the wild life reserve
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does it: one engaged to run the reserve

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager has been told to take charge of a nature park.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MANAGER and WED (the apostrophe adds none) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An official employed to protect and manage animals in a park or estate is this keeper.

clue.text: Peas and carrots are given a star

parts.note: examples of vegetables, informally veg

explanation.surface: Vegetables awarded a top rating on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Point to one duke or another

definitions.text: Point to one duke or another

parts.words: Point to one duke or another
parts.note: the name indicates the famous Iron Duke who beat Napoleon, or any later holder of that ducal title

explanation.surface: An instruction to indicate a particular nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Arthur Wellesley, victor of Waterloo, and of his successors to the dukedom.

clue.text: Cut by a quarter? That's serious

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E (east) is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A cut of a quarter to a budget is a grave matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and serious are synonyms when describing a grave situation or injury.

clue.text: It could be disastrous when I.O.U runs out

indicators.note: out suggests the IOUs being exhausted, but signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the debt note, without the dots

explanation.surface: Debt notes running out could spell financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin, a close synonym of disastrous.

clue.text: Corner at 90

parts.note: a corner measuring ninety degrees, though it reads like a speed or an age

explanation.surface: Taking a corner at ninety miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner of ninety degrees, as in a square, is this geometric term.

clue.text: I'm in prison without money, that's the snag

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the prison word goes around the money

parts.note: pent means penned or imprisoned
a dime is a US coin, standing for money

explanation.surface: Someone jailed and penniless explains their problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the prison word surrounds the money; PENT for prison means penned in.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or hindrance, the same as a snag.

clue.text: Arrangement not laid down?

parts.note: an organisation or system, playfully read as something raised or erected rather than placed lower

explanation.surface: A query about an arrangement not yet fixed in rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is an arrangement or organisation of things.

clue.text: Aunt Sal unexpectedly seen in harem

definitions.note: a phrase describing a woman found there, standing for that woman

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests Aunt Sal's surprising appearance, but signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A family aunt surprisingly turns up in a harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's wife or concubine is one of the women of the harem.

clue.text: Twig a starting price swindle

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
to rig is to fix fraudulently

explanation.surface: Someone realises a betting fix is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like the verb meaning to realise, but is the noun for a small shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shoot or stem of a plant is a sprig, which is much like a twig.

clue.text: Persuade an agency girl to start typing

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency

indicators.note: the start of the word typing, its first letter

explanation.surface: Coaxing a temporary secretary to begin her typing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or persuade someone to do something.

clue.text: Intervals quietly employed in empty talk

indicators.note: the quiet letter is used inside the chatter word

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
P (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Pauses quietly used in idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps are breaks or intervals in time or space.

clue.text: Animal quarters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a female deer, especially a red deer
rear, as in the rear quarters of an animal; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: An animal's lodgings, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a female red deer and an adjective meaning rear, as in an animal's back legs.

clue.text: Jacket cut in style

indicators.note: style here means to fashion or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jacket tailored in a fashionable cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is the indicator, rearranging the letters of CUT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket, as worn in military uniform.

clue.text: Interval elapsing before giving sentence to a convict

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time
a lag is a convict, especially a habitual one

explanation.surface: The delay before a judge sentences a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is the delay that passes between two connected events.

clue.text: Drink in the fresh air next to tents

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed beside the tents word

parts.note: a camp is a collection of tents

indicators.note: fresh suggests open air, but signals the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: Having a drink outdoors beside the campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' simply places the tents word before the reworked air; 'in the' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter Italian aperitif, a brand of drink.

clue.text: A place of current conflict

parts.note: reads like a present-day war zone, but means a spot where opposing water currents clash

explanation.surface: A trouble spot in today's news.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of rough water where opposing tidal currents meet is this phenomenon.

clue.text: Bitterness associated with an age old craft

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
an eon is an age, a vast period

explanation.surface: Resentment linked to an ancient skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a skill but means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, an old vessel.

clue.text: Pet greyhound?

parts.note: a racing hound that runs laps of a track, read as a pampered pet

explanation.surface: A greyhound kept as a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pampered dog kept as a pet is this, punning on a dog that runs laps.

clue.text: Quick, the doctor's in the river!

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the famous African river
MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is a doctor's degree; the 's is a contraction of is

explanation.surface: An urgent cry that a physician has fallen into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble means quick and agile in movement.

clue.text: Tax which makes a difference to cost

indicators.note: changing the word cost signals its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A levy that changes what something costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot is an old word for a tax or levy, surviving in scot-free.

clue.text: Grouse meat

explanation.surface: Game bird served as meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a complaint and the meat of cattle.

clue.text: Their union offers security

parts.note: two items that work together to fasten a door, though union suggests a marriage or trade union

explanation.surface: A partnership that provides stability.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a fastening that is secure, from a device and the item that opens it.

clue.text: Property to come down

definitions.meaning: to alight or touch down, as an aircraft

explanation.surface: Real estate that falls in value.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both owned ground and a verb meaning to come to earth.

clue.text: Going for acquittal

definitions.meaning: leaving, as from a bus or train

explanation.surface: Heading off in pursuit of being cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both alighting from transport and escaping conviction.
